conviction_note: The Q3 TONMYA revenue ($14-15m) and cash ($162.8m) were pre-released on 2026-10-15, so the print turns on things not yet public: the Q3 script count and gross-to-net, opex after the sales force went from 100 to 150 reps, the share count (and so how much ATM was sold), the runway line, and whether the Dr. Reddy's Paragraph IV suit has been filed. The small positives (total revenue slightly above a $16.2-16.3m consensus, wider Medicare coverage, the suit likely filed, a crowded short at negative EV) roughly cancel the small negatives (a launch that looks linear, a bigger loss, governance, the going-concern flag), so impact_sum is +0.4. The scaled number is 53% x 8% = +0.48: the move should be large on a name down 36% in 20 days, and the direction is close to a coin flip.
bar: Q3 2026 total revenue consensus $16.32m (Yahoo, 5 analysts, range $14.88-17.6m, https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TNXP/analysis/) and $16.2m (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TNXP/earnings-forecasts). These two agree; EarningsWhispers' $14.32m is probably TONMYA-only. EPS consensus -$2.24 (Yahoo) to -$2.52 (EW). The company pre-released TONMYA net revenue of $14.0-15.0m on 2026-10-15 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1430306/000149315226047139/form8-k.htm). Add Zembrace/Tosymra at about $2.5m (the Q2 run rate) and implied total revenue is about $16.5-17.5m, roughly +1% to +7% against the bar. The company gives no revenue guidance. The real bar for the reaction is unsourced: the Q4 trajectory and script growth.
positioning_check: Short interest 2,940,708 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement (2,937,499 at 09-30), days to cover 2.41 (https://equibles.com/stocks/tnxp/shortinterest). That is about 17% of the 17.15m shares outstanding and 20.8% of float (https://fintel.io/s/us/tnxp; https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/tnxp/statistics/), so the short is crowded. There is no usable skew: the option chain is unusable (ATM spread 171% of mid, total open interest 757, put/call OI 0.33). On the tape, the stock is -36% over 20 days, -77% from its 52-week high and 1.3% above its 52-week low. It fell steadily from $11.62 (09-15) to $4.69 (11-06), with no single gap, and dropped -10% on 1.2m shares on 2026-11-05 with no news found (Yahoo chart v8). Market cap is about $80m against $162.8m of cash, an enterprise value of about -$95m.

findings.finding: The Q3 TONMYA net revenue pre-release of $14.0-15.0m (+27-36% q/q, after +197% in Q2), plus about $2.5m of Zembrace/Tosymra, implies total Q3 revenue of about $16.5-17.5m against a $16.2-16.3m consensus: a small beat on a number that is already public.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the pre-release day itself (2026-10-15) the stock moved +0.31% per the baseline, then kept falling, from $6.42 to $4.69. Q2 total revenue of $13.5m was 'well above estimates' and bought +4.66% on 2026-08-10. The Q1 report (2026-05-11) fell -5.88%.
findings.why_not_priced: The TONMYA number is priced: it was released 25 days ago. The only unpriced piece is the migraine line and the exact total. If the market had read the pre-release as a beat, the stock would not have fallen 27% after 10-15. It did, so the market reads deceleration, not a beat.
findings.independence: Q2 split from the Q2 release: TONMYA about $11m of $13.5m total, migraine about $2.5m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001430306/000149315226036740/ex99-01.htm). Consensus from Yahoo/Benzinga (see bar). This shares the 10-15 8-K with the financing finding.

findings.finding: Cash fell only $13.4m in Q3 ($176.2m on 06-30 to about $162.8m on 09-30), against H1 operating cash use of $84.6m (about $42m a quarter) and a sales force grown by 50 reps to about 150. Either Q3 burn fell sharply or about $25-30m of ATM stock was sold in Q3. The 10-Q share count (17.15m on 08-07) and an updated runway line (previously 'into early Q2 2027', with a going-concern flag) settle which.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated: the going-concern flag and runway line have been in every 2026 10-Q. The stock fell -5.88% on the Q1 report (2026-05-11), whose 10-Q showed about $20.1m of Q1 ATM issuance (1.41m shares).
findings.why_not_priced: The cash number is public, but the share count and burn split are not. The negative EV (about -$95m) shows the market already assumes heavy dilution and burn. A share count well above about 19.5m, or a shorter runway, would be new bad news. An unchanged count with a lower burn would be new good news. What the money buys is visible: TONMYA revenue went from $3.7m to $11m to $14-15m and the sales force grew by 50%. So this is financing of a ramp, but on a name that carries a going-concern flag.
findings.independence: The Q2 10-Q going-concern note and runway (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001430306/000199937126017452/tnxp-10q_063026.htm). The Q3 cash figure is from the 10-15 8-K (shared with finding 1).

findings.finding: Dr. Reddy's sent a Paragraph IV notice on 2026-10-01 (ANDA for generic TONMYA 2.8mg, challenging all four Orange Book patents). Tonix has 45 days, to about 2026-11-15, to sue and trigger a 30-month stay. No suit appears in EDGAR as of 11-06. Tonix said it 'intends to vigorously enforce' its patents, and confirmation in the Q3 release or call is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The notice was filed 10-02. The stock went from $9.23 (10-01) to $8.07 by 10-05 and to $6.13 by 10-13, part of a -50% October slide, with no other company news found.
findings.why_not_priced: A filed suit (and so the stay to about April 2029) is the expected outcome, so most of it is priced. The residual is timing and any extra detail, such as a forum, other filers, or a settlement-posture comment. If the market treated the suit as certain, the post-notice slide would have partly reversed; it has not. The deadline falls after the window, so the confirmation may land after Nov 9. That probability is netted into the size.
findings.independence: Panabee summary of the notice (https://www.panabee.com/news/tonix-pharmaceuticals-receives-paragraph-iv-notice-for-tonmya). Only one primary document.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-22 a PBM agreement covering about 21m Medicare Part D beneficiaries took effect immediately, lifting TONMYA coverage to about 166m lives from about 136m at the Q2 report. That is about +22% covered lives entering Q4, and Q4/October commentary on the call should show whether it converted.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell on the announcement week: $10.59 on 09-22 to $9.70 on 09-24. A coverage expansion has not been paid for so far.
findings.why_not_priced: The coverage is public. Its effect on October scripts is not, and only the call can show it. Q4 consensus revenue is $19.12m (Yahoo), about +10-15% q/q, which embeds little uplift from it. The stock's slide since suggests the market gives it no credit.
findings.independence: Q2 release: coverage of about 136m lives, and the first managed-Medicare plan effective 2027-01-01 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001430306/000149315226036740/ex99-01.htm).

findings.finding: Opex steps up: Q2 SG&A was $36.0m (vs $16.2m a year earlier) with about 100 reps, and 50 more reps were in the field by September. Q3 SG&A should rise again, against an EPS bar of -$2.24 to -$2.52 that probably embeds part of it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 EPS of -$2.44 'beat' and the stock rose +4.66%. The loss line has not driven reactions on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: The rep expansion was disclosed, but the quarterly cost is not. If the market had priced a loss of about $50m or more, EPS estimates would sit near -$2.7 or below; they sit at -$2.24 to -$2.52, and the share count will also have risen.
findings.independence: Consensus EPS (Yahoo/Benzinga/TipRanks/EW, see bar). This shares the Q2 release with findings 2 and 4.

findings.finding: The launch looks linear rather than accelerating. In Q2, new-patient scripts rose only +36% q/q while refills rose +207%. Q3 TONMYA revenue growth slowed to +27-36% q/q, in line with new-patient growth. Management had guided 'continued fluctuations for gross-to-net in both Q3 and Q4'. The Q3 script count and gross-to-net disclosure are the first numbers that can confirm or break this.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Launch-trajectory disappointments have been sold: 'TNXP Slips After Hours On Slower Than Expected Launch' on the Q1 number (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/tnxp-slips-after-hours-on-slower-than-expected-launch-for-fibromyalgia-drug/cZQ8vF7ReeH), then -4.19% and -5.88% on the Q1 pre-release and report.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference: no Q3 script count exists in public. The -27% slide since the pre-release suggests the market already reads deceleration. What would be new is a gross-to-net deterioration (scripts growing much faster than revenue) or a flat October.
findings.independence: The gross-to-net guidance comes from Q2 call coverage (https://www.stocktaper.com/earningsCallSummary/TNXP/2026/Q2, AI summary, secondary). It shares the Q2 release with findings 2, 4 and 5, and the 10-15 8-K with finding 1.

findings.finding: Governance and strategy: on 2026-11-02 the CEO's son was appointed EVP Strategy and Transformation (effective 10-30), to lead AI-driven cost cuts and business development to 'share development costs' on select pipeline programs. This follows the CEO naming himself interim CMO on 2026-08-18. No savings figures were given. The stock fell -10% on 2026-11-05 on 1.2m shares with no other news found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance. The 11-02 to 11-05 tape went $5.15, $5.19, $5.11, $4.60.
findings.why_not_priced: The governance hit is likely in the -10% of 11-05. What is unpriced is whether the call quantifies cost cuts or names a pipeline partner, which would be positive against a going-concern flag. No evidence exists that it will, so the finding nets to a small negative.
findings.independence: 8-K 2026-08-18 (CEO as interim CMO, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1430306/000149315226039000/form8-k.htm); Pharma Now on the related-party approval (https://www.pharmanow.live/latest-news/tonix-pharmaceuticals-appoints-george-lederman-evp-strategy-transformation).

findings.finding: The short is crowded at negative EV: 2.94m shares short (about 17% of shares outstanding, 20.8% of float, 2.4 days to cover) with market cap about $80m against $162.8m of cash. The stock is 1.3% above its 52-week low after -36% in 20 days, and Canaccord initiated at Buy on 10-26. Any reassuring script, runway or partnering line has a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two most recent full reports rose (+4.66% on 2026-08-10, +4.1% on 2025-11-10). The short has stayed about 2.8-3.6m shares since June while the stock fell, so it has not been covering.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the information set, not a cause. The persistent slide without a gap suggests steady supply (holders exiting, possibly the ATM), and that can continue. Negative EV means the market assumes the cash is burned or diluted away. The squeeze is sized small because the drawdown is partly explained by the Paragraph IV notice, the deceleration and the governance news.
findings.independence: Fintel short float and the Canaccord initiation (https://fintel.io/s/us/tnxp); EV from StockAnalysis (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/tnxp/statistics/).

outside_window.finding: Guggenheim Healthcare Innovation Conference presentation by the CEO, Tuesday 2026-11-10, 16:00-16:25 ET. This is after the window closes at the 11-09 close.

The 45-day Paragraph IV suit deadline is about 2026-11-15. If the suit is filed after 11-09 rather than announced with the print, it lands outside the window. Only the in-window probability is carried in finding 3.
First managed-Medicare plan coverage takes effect 2027-01-01 (about +9m lives). The OASIS acute-stress topline is due mid-2027.
A post-print equity raise is plausible at negative EV with a going-concern flag. If announced after the 11-09 close it falls outside the window. No filing or evidence of one exists.

baseline_tension: No skew is available. The evidence is balanced against a -36% 20-day run-up into a 52-week low with a crowded short, so the run-up and positioning argue for mean reversion while the steady, gap-less supply and the going-concern dilution overhang argue for continuation. I hold p_up at 53, near the non-result.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside a pre-released figure): revenue finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2
Lesson 4 (financing with a going-concern flag): financing finding resigned from +0.3 to -0.1. The money funds a visible ramp, but the going-concern flag stands, so the finding nets to about zero
Lesson 3 (own caveat): the Medicare coverage finding's own text notes the stock fell on the news, so cut from +0.5 to +0.3
Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0, positioning is the information set): squeeze finding cut from +1.0 to +0.5; it is kept because lesson 7 treats a crowded short as a mechanism of its own
Lesson 5 (inference, not a company number): linear-launch finding cut from -0.5 to -0.4
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): p_up moved from 54 to 53; abs_move kept at 8 per lesson 8 (understatement is the systematic error)
